resources.name: Pathoma Chapters 1-3
resources.notes: Universally cited as highest-yield. ~8.5 hours at 1x speed. Watch at 1.5-2x. Re-watch once more in final 2 weeks before exam.
resources.source: 20+ IMG write-ups consistently cite chapters 1-3 as core

resources.name: UWorld (Begin First Pass)
resources.notes: START IMMEDIATELY. Do NOT wait until after content review. Begin system-wise in tutor mode, 20-40 questions/day alongside videos. Multiple IMGs who delayed UWorld regretted it. One said 'doing FA alone is a mistake — you need questions from day 1'.

resources.name: Primary Video Series (B&B OR Bootcamp — pick ONE)
resources.notes: If foundation is weak, use Bootcamp (more detailed). If foundation is okay, use B&B (more concise). Do NOT use both. Watch at 1.5-2x speed. One UK IMG finished all B&B in ~1 month at 1.5-2x. Pair each system's videos with same-system UWorld questions immediately after.
resources.source: Community split but consensus is pick ONE video series

resources.name: First Aid (Core Study Spine)
resources.notes: FA is the structural backbone of every serious USMLE study plan. It is NOT optional. Use it as the organizing spine — each day's study is anchored to specific FA page ranges by system. First pass: read FA section for each system alongside video lectures and UWorld questions for that system. Second pass: review weak sections identified by NBME analysis. Rapid Review section (pages 670-688) in the final week before exam. Total: 636 pages across 17 sections. Do NOT read cover-to-cover passively — always pair with active questions. Annotate sparingly — one color for UWorld pearls, one for personal weak points. Edition: use latest available, but older editions (2023/2024) are adequate.
resources.source: Every structured study plan analyzed (7-mo, 8-mo, 9-mo, 1-yr variants) uses FA page numbers as the daily progress unit. Universal across all plan architectures.

resources.name: Sketchy Micro
resources.notes: Called 'gold' by multiple IMGs. Non-negotiable. Pair with AnKing Sketchy Micro tags in Anki. One IMG took ~2 months watching 2-3 videos/day.
resources.source: Universal agreement that Sketchy Micro is essential

resources.name: Sketchy Pharm
resources.notes: Highly recommended but some IMGs use Pixorize instead. Longer than Micro (~30 min per video). 4-6 weeks if doing many per day. Pair with AnKing Pharm tags. Some IMGs called Sketchy Pharm the 'worst of the 3' but still useful.
resources.source: Most IMGs use it; some substitute Pixorize

resources.name: Sketchy Path
resources.notes: OPTIONAL. Most IMGs skip this. Consensus: Micro=must, Pharm=recommended, Path=optional. Only do if you have surplus time.
resources.source: Multiple IMGs say it's least useful

resources.name: Anki (AnKing Deck with UWorld + Sketchy tags)
resources.notes: Start Day 1. Use AnKing deck filtered by: Sketchy Micro tags, Sketchy Pharm tags, and UWorld tags. Do NOT unsuspend the entire deck. Working IMGs: 50-80 new cards/day max. Reviews will pile to 300-500/day at peak. Stop adding NEW cards 1-2 weeks before exam. Focus final weeks on reviews only. One IMG said 'AnKing with UWorld tags is the best use'.

resources.name: Pathoma (Full - Chapters 4+)
resources.notes: Watch once at 1.5-2x alongside the relevant system in your video series. Total Pathoma is ~25 hours at 1x. System chapters are lower yield than 1-3 but still worth one pass. Integrate with FA pathology sections.
resources.source: Most IMGs watch once, don't re-watch system chapters

resources.name: UWorld Second Pass (Incorrects + Flagged)
resources.notes: After completing first pass, do all incorrect + flagged questions. One IMG did ~1300 questions in second pass and raised accuracy from 40% to 60%. Some IMGs do full reset if time permits, but incorrects-only is the minimum. Do in random timed mode.
resources.source: Most successful IMGs do a second pass

resources.name: First NBME (Baseline)
resources.notes: Take FIRST NBME once UWorld is 50%+ complete. DO NOT take earlier — low scores before sufficient prep cause demoralization without useful data. Use an older form (25 or 26) as baseline. Expect 50-60% on first attempt. This is NORMAL for IMGs. One IMG scored 46% on first NBME and eventually passed.
resources.source: Multiple IMGs regret taking NBMEs too late OR too early

resources.name: NBME Series (Weekly in Final 6-8 Weeks)
resources.notes: Take NBMEs 25-31 roughly weekly. Newer forms (25-31) reflect current content. After each NBME: spend 2-3 days analyzing every question. Categorize misses into 'knowledge gaps', 'trick questions', and 'carelessness'. Map misses to systems and use that to drive next week's UWorld blocks. Target: mid-60s to 70%+ on multiple forms before sitting for exam.
resources.source: Universal recommendation; one IMG took 25-33 weekly

resources.name: Free 120 (New Version)
resources.notes: Take 3-7 days before exam under Prometric-like conditions. One IMG said the new Free 120 felt 'incredibly representative of the real deal'. Target: 70%+. This is your final readiness check.
resources.source: Consistent recommendation; new Free 120 highly valued

resources.name: Dirty Medicine / Randy Neil (Biochem, Ethics, Biostats)
resources.notes: OPTIONAL but frequently cited as helpful for specific topics: biochemistry pathways, inheritance patterns, ethics, biostats. Watch at 1.5x on low-energy days or during commute. One IMG: 'Dirty medicine for biochem is gold if you supplement with Mehlman PDF'. NOT a replacement for core resources.
resources.source: Cited by ~40% of IMG write-ups as helpful supplement

resources.name: Divine Intervention Podcast
resources.notes: Passive review during commute/exercise. One IMG listened to ~180 episodes on biochem/ethics topics. Good for low-energy days when active study isn't possible. Not mandatory.
resources.source: Cited by some IMGs; useful for passive review

gatingRules.message: Complete at least 50% of UWorld before your first NBME. Taking it earlier risks demoralization without useful data.
You have more than 3 active resources. Every IMG who failed cited resource overload. Pause one before adding another.
Wait at least 5 days between NBMEs. You need time to analyze mistakes and remediate, not just test repeatedly.

gatingRules.warning: You've been studying for 3+ weeks but completed fewer than 50 FA pages. FA works best when read actively alongside UWorld — try pairing each FA section with matching UWorld questions instead of reading alone.
Stop adding new Anki cards. Final 2 weeks should be reviews only. Protect what you already know.

gatingRules.message: Take the new Free 120 this week under exam-like conditions. This is your final readiness check.
